item: 4.7 dontAsk mode — displayed when the CLI reports it, never offered; a first run seeds the chip from system/init (2026-09-04)
branch: The mode menu carries a `Don't ask` row that is [hidden] unless dontAsk is the current mode. applyCliMode's unknown-mode guard therefore ACCEPTS a `permissionMode:"dontAsk"` broadcast (chip + #app[data-mode] follow it, the row shows), and the next broadcast of any other mode hides the row again. With nothing persisted Kotlin pushes no stored __mode; the chip is seeded by the same __mode frame carrying the CLI's `initialize` `current_permission_mode` (ChatPanel.pushInitMeta), which `system/init` repeats with the first turn — the frame this fixture feeds
provenance: `system/init` and `system/status` carrying `permissionMode` is the CLI's shape (docs/ide-mcp-protocol.md § permission facts; init frame copied from fixture 40). The value `dontAsk` was MEASURED on 2.1.260 (2026-09-04): `--permission-mode dontAsk` and a settings-file `permissions.defaultMode:"dontAsk"` both make init report `dontAsk` verbatim (no `default`-style alias), and `--permission-mode` beats the file — which is why the panel omits the flag until a mode is picked. The display-only rule is VS Code 2.1.260's (`webview/index.js` c4(): dontAsk is unshifted into the picker only while current). Negative control: on the pre-4.7 build no dontAsk row exists, so the guard drops the broadcast — data-mode stays manual, the chip keeps reading Manual and the row query returns null; those asserts are DISCRIMINATING, step 1's mode asserts are GUARDS (plan seeded via init already worked).

steps.note: first run: no stored __mode, the CLI's own mode broadcast seeds the chip

expect.why: GUARD: with no persisted mode the init broadcast alone moves the chip off its markup default
GUARD: the chip names the CLI's mode

expect.js: (function(){ var i = document.querySelector('#modeMenu .popup-item[data-v="dontAsk"]'); return i ? i.hidden : 'absent'; })()
expect.why: DISCRIMINATING: the Don't-ask row exists but is hidden while another mode is current (pre-fix: absent)

steps.note: the CLI reports dontAsk (a settings-file defaultMode on a first run): chip, accent and the row follow

expect.why: DISCRIMINATING: the guard accepts dontAsk because a row exists for it (pre-fix: stays manual — the chip lied)
DISCRIMINATING: the chip names the mode the CLI is actually in

expect.js: (function(){ var i = document.querySelector('#modeMenu .popup-item[data-v="dontAsk"]'); return i ? i.hidden : 'absent'; })()
expect.why: DISCRIMINATING: the row is shown while dontAsk is current — so the menu can say where you are

expect.js: (function(){ var i = document.querySelector('#modeMenu .popup-item[data-v="dontAsk"]'); return i ? i.classList.contains('on') : 'absent'; })()
expect.why: GUARD: it carries the check like any current mode (null-safe so the pre-fix build reports 'absent' instead of aborting the run)
GUARD: five visible rows now — the four offered modes plus the displayed one

steps.note: leaving dontAsk (any later broadcast) hides the row again — a one-way exit, as in VS Code

expect.why: GUARD: the status broadcast moves the chip

expect.js: (function(){ var i = document.querySelector('#modeMenu .popup-item[data-v="dontAsk"]'); return i ? i.hidden : 'absent'; })()
expect.why: DISCRIMINATING: the row hides the moment another mode is current — it cannot be picked back (pre-fix: absent)
GUARD: back to the four offered modes
